{{Quote|The chief's dead. They're all dead. What were those things?|Diyaz|<ref name="Striking Back" />}}
In [[3643 BBY]], during the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Angral]]'s [[Desolator crisis|personal war]] against the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] amid the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] between the Republic and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reconstituted Sith Empire]], a number of [[Mark II Power Guard]]s&mdash;advanced [[Cybernetics/Legends|cybernetically]]-augmented [[Soldier/Legends|supersoldiers]]&mdash;'''attacked''' a [[SIS safe house|safe house]] on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]]. The safe house belonged to the [[Republic Strategic Information Service]], and the [[Power Guard Enhancement System|Power Guards]] had been sent by the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Sadic]], who had [[Torture/Legends|tortured]] the location of the safe house out of SIS [[Agent/Legends|Agent]] [[Galen (SIS)|Galen]]. The Power Guards [[Death/Legends|killed]] several agents, but the arrival of a [[Hero of Tython|young Jedi Knight]] only [[Standard minute/Legends|minutes]] into the attack saved the lives of the remaining agents, as the Knight dispatched the Power Guards.

==Prelude==
{{Quote|Bring the datapad back to headquarters. My slicers will crack the decryption.|Rieekan|<ref name="Striking Back" />}}
In [[3643 BBY]],<ref name="Time" /> during the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]], the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Angral]] declared a [[Desolator crisis|personal war]] against the Republic after the [[Death/Legends|death]] of his [[Gender/Legends|son]], [[Tarnis (Sith Lord)|Tarnis]]. Using stolen information on the [[Republic superweapon initiative]], Angral dispatched his [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentices]] to seize control of several Republic [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] programs.<ref name="Race to the Ruins">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Race to the Ruins|Coruscant}}</ref> One of Angral's apprentices, [[Sadic]], was tasked with acquiring the [[Power Guard Enhancement System]], a [[Soldier/Legends|supersoldier]] program of [[Adrenal/Legends|adrenal]] stimulants and [[Cybernetics/Legends|cybernetics]] that was based on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]].<ref name="Red Light" /> Not long after Sadic's forces successfully located and took control of the project, [[Agent/Legends|Agent]] [[Galen (SIS)|Galen]] of the [[Republic Strategic Information Service]]&mdash;the Republic's intelligence agency&mdash;arrived on Nar Shaddaa and attempted to track down the project himself. Galen was soon captured by Sadic, who subjected the [[operative]] to the Power Guard process and also [[Torture/Legends|tortured]] him to extract information on the SIS's operations on the moon.<ref name="Showdown" />

A [[Hero of Tython|young Jedi Knight]] soon arrived on Nar Shaddaa in search of both Galen and the project, and, with the aid of the SIS branch under [[Bureau Chief]] [[Rieekan (SIS)|Rieekan]], the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] was able to locate the main [[Power Guard Cybernetics Lab]]. After [[Skirmish in the Power Guard Cybernetics Lab|dispatching]] the Imperials guarding the facility, the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] recovered an encrypted [[Datapad/Legends|datapad]] that could provide clues as to where Sadic had moved the project, so Rieekan asked the Knight to bring the datapad back to the [[SIS safe house]] in the [[Promenade]] shopping complex. However, Sadic dispatched a trio of [[Mark II Power Guard]]s to the safe house, intending to put an end to their meddling in his affairs.<ref name="Striking Back" />

==The raid==
{{Quote|They knew our passcodes and overrides. Took them only seconds to get down here.|Diyaz|<ref name="Striking Back" />}}
The Power Guards entered [[Gudnem's Gadget Emporium]], the store that the safe house used as a front, and [[Death/Legends|killed]] the staff before using Galen's passcodes and overrides to access the rear [[Turbolift/Legends|turbolift]] that led to the safe house. The Power Guards quickly overwhelmed the surprised SIS agents within the safe house, and Rieekan was killed in the [[Lightfight|firefight]]. The Jedi Knight arrived [[Standard minute/Legends|minutes]] after the Power Guards, and, upon finding several Power Guards still in Gudnem's Gadget Emporium, the Knight and a companion cut down the mind-controlled supersoldiers and headed down to the safe house. They were just in [[Time/Legends|time]] to stop the Power Guards from killing the last of the agents, including [[Special Agent/Legends|Special Agent]] [[Korol Tander]] and Agent [[Diyaz]].<ref name="Striking Back" />

==Aftermath==
{{Quote|With Rieekan dead, I'm acting bureau chief. This operation's over. Agent Diyaz, we're leaving now. Sorry, friend, but you're on your own.|Tander|<ref name="Showdown" />}}
{{GameLS|Star Wars: The Old Republic}}
With the heavy losses among the SIS staff, Tander wanted to pull out entirely, but the Knight convinced Diyaz to decrypt the datapad anyway, and Diyaz traced the Power Guard project to a [[Imperial weapons factory]] in the [[Lower Industrial Sector]].<ref name="Striking Back" /> Diyaz planted a [[Homing beacon/Legends|tracker]] on the Knight as the Jedi left to take out the factory, and, though the remaining SIS agents abandoned the safe house, Tander also contacted [[General/Legends|General]] [[Var Suthra]], who sent in the special operations [[Squad/Legends|unit]] [[Blackstar Squad]] to help destroy the Power Guard project.<ref name="Showdown" />
{{Endgame}}

The loss of the safe house was a severe blow to SIS operations on the moon, to the point that [[Director of Republic Strategic Information Service|SIS Director]] [[Marcus Trant]] was notified of the loss, and he used the attack as a cautionary tale a [[Standard week/Legends|week]] later when permitting Agent [[Theron Shan]] to pursue a [[Mission to the Vesla system|mission]] into Imperial [[Realspace/Legends|space]].<ref name="Lost Suns">[[The Old Republic — The Lost Suns 2|''The Old Republic — The Lost Suns'' 2]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Sorry, friend, but I'm in charge here now.|The Knight, after punching Tander in the face|<ref name="Striking Back" />}}
The attack on the SIS safe house was first mentioned in the [[The Old Republic — The Lost Suns 2|second issue]] of [[Star Wars: The Old Republic — The Lost Suns|''The Lost Suns'']] [[Star Wars comic books|comic-book]] miniseries that tied into the then-upcoming [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''. The issue was released on [[July 20]], [[2011]], and written by [[Alexander Freed]]<ref name="Lost Suns" /> five months before ''The Old Republic''{{'s}} release. The actual attack then appeared in the Jedi Knight-class mission "Striking Back" on Nar Shaddaa in ''The Old Republic''.<ref name="Striking Back" />

After the attack, the player has three options to convince Tander and Diyaz: ask Tander to stay, [[Mind trick/Legends|Force Persuade]] him, or punch him. Harming Tander results in [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark-side]] alignment points, but as the Jedi Knight is a Republic class and thus assumed to choose those options that reward the player with the maximum [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light-side]] alignment points, this article assumes that the player did not attack Tander.<ref name="Striking Back" />
